noEntry.heading: No directory entry
noEntry.text: You are signed in as {name}, and there is no person of that name in this realm's directory. A certificate issued over ACME, EST or SCEP always names an entry and is kept on it, so there is nothing to issue to until one exists.
other.heading: Other certificates
other.before: A TLS client certificate this portal issues you directly, and your RFC 7523 and RFC 7522 signing keys, are on
other.after: . This page is about the three enrollment protocols a client or a device speaks to get one.
fresh.eabHeading: Your new ACME account binding key
fresh.eabCopy: Copy it now. The HMAC key is shown on this page once and cannot be shown again.
fresh.eabNote: The key binds ONE account, and that account can only ever be issued certificates for you.
fresh.challengeCopy: Copy it now. It is shown on this page once and cannot be shown again.
fresh.challengeNote: It is spent by the first certificate request that uses it, and that certificate names you.
enrolled.heading: Your enrolled certificates
enrolled.none: You hold no certificate issued over ACME, EST or SCEP.
enrolled.note: Revoking puts the certificate on its authority's CRL and makes OCSP answer revoked. It cannot be undone.
acme.text: An ACME client registers an account at {url} with an External Account Binding key; the account is then bound to you for life.
acme.make: Make an ACME account binding key
est.text: An EST client authenticates with your username and password (or a certificate you were issued over EST, ACME or SCEP) and posts a certificate request. Nothing needs to be made here first.
scep.text: A SCEP client puts a challenge password in its certificate request to {url}. Each is for one profile and is spent once.
hostNames.heading: Host names registered to you
hostNames.note: A TLS server certificate names only these. An administrator registers them; this service never proves control of a name by contacting it.
